A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with complete main text and Appendices A-D. Text comparison and rendered-page checks support reliable comparison of the equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training experiments across 23 data recipes, including ranking correlations, decision regret, and supplementary analyses in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their results in Section 6 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: Both versions propose training proxy models with tiny learning rates and ranking data recipes by validation loss. The procedure and learning-rate selection guidance are unchanged.

E1.justification: The same 23 recipes cover domain composition, established corpora, quality filtering, and deduplication. Pile validation domains, the five downstream benchmarks, and appendix test scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: The standard-learning-rate proxy comparisons in Figures 5-6 and the accumulated-gradient-alignment comparison in Figure 28 retain the same comparators. No comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 and Appendix D retain the same model configurations, single-epoch training, token budgets, dataset-specific target-model tuning, evaluation metrics, and supplementary experimental protocols.

E4.justification: The learning-rate-bound validation, batch-size and weight-decay ablations, overtraining analysis, recipe-specific learning-rate curves, gradient-alignment analysis, and early-stopping/warmup experiments are all retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard errors across three seeds in Figure 3 and 95% bootstrap confidence intervals from resampling seeds in Figure 6 and corresponding appendix figures. Run-count and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported values and findings are unchanged, including Figure 3's ranking reversal and Figure 4(a)'s Spearman correlation of 0.97. All embedded figure images, including the supplementary results, are identical between versions.

T1.justification: The random-feature-model assumptions, theorem statements, and proofs in Section 5.2 and Appendix B are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same learning-rate-bound derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about proxy-ranking fragility, assessing recipes under dataset-specific tuning, and improving transferability through tiny learning rates.

C2.justification: The gradient-alignment and higher-order-effect explanations are unchanged, as are discussions of stochasticity, numerical precision, single-epoch scope, and limitations concerning architecture selection, multi-epoch training, and curricula.

D1.justification: Appendix D retains identical optimizer settings, tuning grids, scheduling, precision, hardware, evaluation instructions, and recipe thresholds. No implementation or resource-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The references and research positioning, including Appendix A's extended related work and discussion of DataDecide, are unchanged.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Preprint' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026', and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Scientific wording and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3 and its caption move slightly upward on page 4, and the continuing paragraph below Figure 4 on page 5 is rewrapped. Figure content, captions, tables, and the remaining body layout are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 updates publication information and makes small layout adjustments on pages 4-5. The scientific content, evidence, proofs, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, yielding no meaningful overall quality difference.
